# Take it apart {#paper background-color="#f0674d"}

Your paper, with its data. The agent finds the biggest problem and tries to fix
it, while we do something else.

## It worked for me

- I did this with a recent paper in my own field.
- It found a real problem, then a new estimator: valid under weaker assumptions,
  and better than the one in the paper.
- My only input was pushing.
- At Strategy in October, this was the exercise that landed. **The catch was
  waiting for it.** So today, we don't wait.

## Where your time goes

```{=html}
{{< include images/paper-time.svg >}}
```

You know the field. **The agent does the reading; you do the judging.**

## Before you leave it alone {#mode}

It will want to run code. If it stops to ask, it waits for you while you're away.

- **Switch the mode** under the prompt box to *Accept edits* (it still asks before
  other commands) or *Auto* (it asks only when something looks risky).
- **It works in this folder,** and you have a save point. Anything it does, you
  can undo.
- Asked to install Python or R? Say yes before you go.

## Start it {#start .your-turn background-color="#f1c84b"}

::: {.prompt}
Take this paper apart, like a tough methods referee who also has the data. Run the
analysis yourself and check that the numbers in the draft match the code. If there
is a preregistration, compare the paper with it. Find the single biggest problem,
then propose a fix and show what changes. Write everything to take-apart.md. Work
on your own; I'll be back in 20 minutes.
:::

Then leave it. **Next: [It wants to please you](sycophancy.html).**

## When you're back {#back}

Read `take-apart.md`. Then push:

- *"Show me where in the paper, and where in the code."*
- *"Rerun it the way the preregistration says."*
- *"Is that really the biggest problem?"*
- *"Show that the fix works."*

**Interviews, not data?** *"Which claims rest on the fewest interviews?"* *"What
else would explain the same quotes?"*

## Round-up {#roundup}

- Best problem found?
- Did it find something **good** for the paper?
- Worst false alarm?
- **Keep the folder.** The referees get the paper next, but not the folder.

**Next: [the blind referee panel](review.html).**
